title: RLTL;DR: Self-Improvement by Internalizing Self-Generated Feedback
gist: Apple researchers (NeurIPS paper) propose RLTL;DR, where a policy writes a one-line TL;DR insight after each failed attempt using verifier output and then internalizes a task-to-insight mapping, breaking through tasks where standard GRPO stays at 0-1% Pass@1. A stripped-down SFTL;DR variant trained on only 4k (task, insight) tuples nearly matches full RLTL;DR and SFT on full rollouts.

themes.theme: RLVR hits a wall on zero-success tasks

insights.claim: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) optimizes toward successful attempts, so it breaks down for self-improvement on tasks where the agent has little or no chance of success and no teacher model or example solutions exist.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Standard RL scaling has a ceiling on frontier-hard tasks; methods that bootstrap from failure are key to continued capability gains without stronger teachers.
insights.quote: This becomes problematic in the realms of self-improvement, where tasks are so difficult that the agent has a low or even no chance of success
insights.locator: The common paradigm of reinforcement learning

insights.claim: On tool-calling and coding datasets filtered to Pass@128 = 0, standard GRPO training of a Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking policy stayed flat at 0-1% Pass@1.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Quantifies the learning barrier for GRPO-style RL on hard tasks, the dominant post-training recipe industry-wide.
insights.quote: standard GRPO training of a Qwen 3.5 9B Thinking policy stays flat at a Pass@1 of 0% to 1%
insights.locator: On challenging tool-calling and coding datasets

insights.claim: RLTL;DR shows the policy the verifier output after each failed attempt, has it write a single TL;DR insight, conditions subsequent rollouts on all prior insights, and samples sequentially until a solution is found.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Converts failures into dense learning signal, potentially reducing dependence on costly teacher models or human-written solutions.
insights.quote: After each failed attempt, we show the policy the verifier outputs and let it write its own feedback, in the form of a single TL;DR insight.
insights.locator: In this paper, we introduce RLTL;DR

insights.claim: RLTL;DR lifted Pass@1 to 14-31% with insights in context during training and 12-13% with no insight in context at evaluation, versus 0-1% for GRPO.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Gains persist without inference-time scaffolding, meaning the capability is baked into weights at no extra serving cost.
insights.quote: achieving a Pass@1 of 14–31% with insights in context during training and, crucially, 12–13% when no insight is in context at eval time
insights.locator: RLTL;DR breaks through this learning barrier

insights.claim: The authors identify backpropagating on in-context insights to internalize a direct task-to-insight mapping as the key driver of RLTL;DR's gains.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Points to distilled meta-knowledge, not raw rollouts, as the valuable training asset.
insights.quote: We identify that the key is the task → insight internalization.

insights.claim: SFTL;DR, which trains only on (task, insight) tuples without showing or backpropagating on any rollouts, recovers almost the full performance of RLTL;DR and classical SFT on full rollouts using just 4k tuples.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Suggests far cheaper post-training: short insight tuples may substitute for expensive full-trajectory data, pressuring the value of large rollout/trace datasets.
insights.quote: Training on only 4k of these tuples recovers almost the full performance of RLTL;DR and classical SFT on full rollouts.

insights.claim: The authors propose a compacted training paradigm of the form 'on this sort of task, keep this sort of thing in mind' as a direction for future research.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: If adopted, compute and data costs of post-training small models could fall sharply, favoring on-device AI efforts.
insights.quote: This demonstrates a promising compacted training paradigm of the form “on this sort of task, keep this sort of thing in mind”
